title: tk config migrate should warn structurally, not per-key, when routing crosses kinds
description:
Follow-up qf0 identified while fixing the reader. The reader now refuses a role whose kind is not pi, but tk config migrate is unchanged: it still warns only about WHICH VALUE WON, never about WHICH READER the winning value is for, so it will merrily merge a ## Pi Orchestrator block into a claude [roles] table again and produce a config the reader then refuses.

Now that the refusal exists, the migrator can cheaply emit the structural warning instead of six per-key ones: "these keys came from a pi-only block and are being merged into a [roles] table whose kind is claude — the pi extension will refuse this config". That turns a confusing downstream refusal into an explanation at the point of migration.
